relevance_note: Single-patient case report of LAD-I with ITGB2 variants: "Two variants, namely c.533C>T, p.Pro178Leu and c.59-1G>A (NM_000211.5, NP_000202.3) in the ITGB2 gene, were identified".
method_note: Read by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON. Table 1 has patients as columns: column 1 header 'Khandewal et al. (21)' (text spells 'Khandelwal'), column 2 header 'Neven et al. (9)', column 3 header 'Patient' (the present case, labelled 'patient' by rule 5 so the label matches the text). The two previously published patients (Table 1 columns 1 and 2) are in scope as LAD-I patients with individual-level facts; no variant, sex or age at onset is printed for them, so they have no variant rows. Age at HCT is not a schema field; it is noted in treatment_summary. Parents included as tested relatives (each carries one of the proband's variants per parental sequencing); their zygosity is not stated, so 'not reported'. The mother's age (21-year-old) comes from the donor row of Table 1 and was recorded as age at last evaluation. Contradiction: Table 1 gives 'Infectious complications pre-HCT' as 'No' for the present patient, while the text reports recurrent omphalitis and repeated bacterial infections before HCT; both rows are emitted. The checklist item 'omphalitis' was kept 'observed' because the table addresses the umbrella category, not omphalitis specifically. Umbilical cord separation 'at 14 days of life' is not called delayed by the paper, so 'delayed umbilical cord separation' is 'not reported'. VOD/SOS excluded for the two prior patients from the explicit statement about the three Table 1 cases ('none but the present case developed VOD/SOS'). Functional evidence (CD18 flow cytometry) is the patient's own result and reflects both variants together; it is recorded on both of her variant rows. Variant type 'splice' for c.59-1G>A comes from the authors' statement that it was 'considered to cause splicing abnormalities'; c.533C>T has no stated class. Pathogenicity for c.533C>T is the authors' citation of an earlier report ('reported to be pathogenic (13)'). No stacked cells.

treatment_summary.value: IV antibiotics for each omphalitis episode; prophylactic trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole; surgical excision of the urachal remnant at 10 months; HLA-haploidentical HCT at 12 months from her 21-year-old mother (PBSC) after RIC (alemtuzumab, fludarabine, AUC-targeted busulfan) with PT-CY, tacrolimus and MMF; topical steroids for skin GVHD; ganciclovir for CMV viremia; voriconazole; defibrotide for VOD/SOS; immunoglobulin supplementation until 3 months post-HCT
span: each of which was treated with intravenous (IV) antibiotics
Prophylactic antimicrobial therapy with trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole was initiated. The patient underwent surgical excision of the urachal remnant when she was 10 months old.
| Age at HCT | 15 months | 3 months | 12 months |
GVHD prophylaxis included PT-CY 50 mg/kg IV on days +3 and +4, followed by tacrolimus continuous IV and oral mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) started on day +5.
The patient required immunoglobulin supplementation until 3 months post-HCT.
